instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

Halve the onion and peel the 4 garlic cloves. Put them on the sheet with the 6 tomatoes, drizzle everything with a little oil and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the tomato skins have split and blackened in spots.

Meanwhile, pull the stems off 2 guajillo chiles and shake out the seeds. Put them in a bowl, cover them with hot water from the kettle and leave them for 15 to 20 minutes, until they're soft and bend easily.
While everything roasts, cut each of the 12 tortillas into 6 wedges. Tortillas that are a day or two old fry up crisper. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro and crumble the 4 oz cotija.

Pour about 1/4 inch of oil into a large skillet and heat it over medium high, until a tortilla wedge sizzles hard as soon as it goes in. Fry the wedges in batches, turning them once, for 2 to 3 minutes a batch, until they're golden and crisp. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Lift the chips onto a plate lined with paper towels and sprinkle them with 1/4 tsp of the salt.

Drain the guajillos. Put them in a blender with the roasted tomatoes, onion and garlic and any juice from the sheet. Add the 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp oregano and 3/4 tsp of the salt and blend until smooth. The vegetables are hot, so hold a towel over the lid while it runs.
Carefully pour off all but a thin film of oil from the skillet. Set it over medium and pour in the sauce. It'll sizzle. Simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens a little.
Taste the sauce, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Add the chips and toss them until they're all coated. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the chips have softened at the edges. Take them off sooner if you like some crunch left.

Meanwhile, heat a thin film of oil in a nonstick skillet over medium. Crack in the 4 eggs, sprinkle them with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Divide the chilaquiles among 4 plates and put an egg on each. Top them with the cotija, 1/4 cup of the crema and the cilantro. Serve with hot sauce on the side.
method_notes: All three versions fry or bake corn tortilla wedges until crisp, make a red salsa from tomatoes, onion, garlic and dried guajillo, then simmer the chips in it briefly and top them with fresh cheese and crema. Tasting Table roasts the tomatoes, onion and garlic at 450°F, blends them with soaked guajillos, paprika, oregano and a sazón packet, and cooks the chips in the salsa for about 5 minutes. Maricruz Avalos simmers the tomatoes and chiles instead of roasting them and adds cumin, black pepper and chicken bouillon, and Mission Food bakes the chips and peels the tomatoes. Both of those top each plate with a fried egg, which this one does too, and this one leaves out the sazón packet.
